body_ar:
الحث على تسهيل الحلال ما موقف الناس اتجاه ذويهم ومجتمعاتهم الذين ينتهجون في شؤون الزواج مناهج يعسر معها لغير الغني أو الكبير الزواج وبماذا تنصحونه؟

أن من العادات السيئة الموروثة عن مجتمع البادية السعي لصعوبة الحلال وتسهيل الحرام، وهذه العادة دارجة في كثير من المجتمعات، فالحرام سهل لأن الحضانة لا تكون على الوجه الشرعي المرضي، ولأن الاختلاط سائد، فالحرام سهل جدا في المجتمعات السائبة، والحلال صعب جدا لكثرة الضوابط والشروط والعادات وهذا مناف للشرع، فالحلال هو الذي ينبغي تسهيله وإشاعته، والحرام هو الذي ينبغي السد دونه بالكلية وإزالته.
body_en:
Urging that the lawful be made easy. What is people's position towards their own families and their societies, who follow, in the matter of marriage, approaches that make marriage difficult for anyone who is not rich or not advanced in years? And what do you advise them?

Among the bad customs inherited from the society of the desert interior is the striving to make the lawful difficult and the forbidden easy. This custom is current in many societies. The forbidden is easy, because the rearing of children is not on the footing the Sharia approves, and because the mixing of the sexes is prevalent; so the forbidden is very easy in unrestrained societies, while the lawful is very difficult, because of the multitude of restrictions and conditions and customs. This is contrary to the Sharia: it is the lawful that ought to be made easy and made widespread, and the forbidden that ought to be blocked off entirely and removed.

flags.arabic: لأن الحضانة لا تكون على الوجه الشرعي المرضي
flags.context: فالحرام سهل لأن الحضانة لا تكون على الوجه الشرعي المرضي، ولأن الاختلاط سائد
options: because the rearing of children is not on the footing the Sharia approves
because custody of children is not on the footing the Sharia approves
because the guarding [of women] is not on the footing the Sharia approves
flags.note: The glossary fixes ḥaḍānah as 'custody', its technical sense in family law — the right and duty of physical care of a child after a marriage ends. That technical sense does not fit here: the Sheikh is explaining why illicit relations are easy in these societies, and is pointing to how the young are brought up and supervised, not to a rule about post-divorce custody. Option 2 reads ḥaḍānah as the guarding of women, which some Mauritanian usage would allow and which fits the pairing with ikhtilāṭ, but is not the word's standard sense. The Sheikh's office should confirm which is meant.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. A .docx download is offered after this single question and answer ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The answer itself is a completed argument and does not break off mid-clause, but the page is one entry of a compilation. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

'The society of the desert interior' renders mujtamaʿ al-bādiyah. The Sheikh is speaking of his own society's inherited custom and the English keeps that self-reference; 'bedouin' has been avoided as carrying associations in English that the Arabic does not.
'Unrestrained societies' renders al-mujtamaʿāt al-sāʾibah, societies in which the young are left to themselves without supervision. It is a strong term in the Arabic and has not been softened.
'Blocked off entirely' renders al-sadd dūnahu bi-l-kulliyyah, an echo of the Maliki principle of blocking the means to harm (sadd al-dharāʾiʿ), though the Sheikh does not name the principle here.
